candidate_relations.reason: A painless superolateral extraconal cyst at the frontozygomatic suture with smooth remodeling, T2 hyperintensity, FLAIR hypointensity, and no enhancement is a dermoid cyst.
There was no pain, fever, or inflammatory signs, and the mass is a well-circumscribed non-enhancing cyst rather than cellulitis.
Orbital lymphangioma is typically multilocular with septa or blood products, unlike this unilocular suture-based non-enhancing cyst.
Neurofibroma should be solid and enhancing, whereas this lesion is fluid-attenuating without internal enhancement or diffusion restriction.
A supraorbital-nerve schwannoma would enhance and follow the nerve, not present as a non-enhancing FLAIR-hypointense cyst remodeling the suture.
Colloid cyst is the wrong histology and typical location for a superolateral frontozygomatic remodeling cyst in a child.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: colloid vs dermoid histology at suture

candidate_relations.reason: A lacrimal-gland ductal cyst sits in gland parenchyma, whereas this mass is centered on the frontozygomatic suture with bone remodeling.
Hemangioma enhances and is vascular; MRI showed no internal enhancement or diffusion restriction in a fluid-content cyst.
Orbital dermoid is the same lesion specified to the extraconal superolateral compartment that compressed the rectus muscles.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: orbital site of the same dermoid

candidate_relations.reason: Lymphangioma would not be a solitary suture-adjacent cyst with smooth osseous scalloping and completely absent internal enhancement.
